comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Settled. One thread and ~48 KB per pane, idle at zero CPU, measured at fifteen panes against a real daemon (observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 11, 'What sixteen of them cost'). Both questions answered: thread-per-watcher stays, and the upstream ask (a_27N6pklkl) drops from need to courtesy - Muster ships the sidebar without it.

What the measurement found that nobody asked for: a watcher costs two descriptors, not one, because watch() clones the stream so Drop can unpark the thread. Against the 256 a GUI-launched process inherits from launchd, fifteen panes on two daemons is a real fraction of the budget - raised as a_28MLhxLsn.

The rig is crates/muster-perf/examples/watcher-cost.rs: an example rather than a baseline entry, so the gate compiles it and never fails a build over a memory reading.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Agent state costs one held-open connection and one thread per pane (observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 11). At 15 panes that is 16 of each, and nothing has measured what it costs in memory, file descriptors or scheduling.

The number decides two things: whether the upstream ask (a_27N6pklkl) is worth pressing, and whether the current thread-per-watcher shape should become one thread polling many sockets. Needs the splits work first, since that is what puts 15 panes in a window.
title: 📊 Budget the per-pane agent connections at 15 panes
